summary: A 100-foot steel fire tower on the De Soto National Forest, no longer in service and kept by the Forest Service for emergencies.

facts.design: 100-foot International Derrick Co. steel tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab

events.note: Congress bought the University Forest Lands tract for the De Soto National Forest; the tower came with it
Registered as NHLR US 525 (MS 5) on July 24, 2003

evidence.supports: tower design: 100-foot steel tower, 7x7 metal cab; no build date given
evidence.quote: a 100’ International Derrick Co. steel tower with 7’x7’ metal cab

evidence.supports: Navy land, virgin longleaf timber for ship masts
evidence.quote: Once the U.S. Navy owned 23,000 acres of land in southern Mississippi to provide virgin longleaf timber for ships masts.

evidence.supports: land transferred to state as endowment for University of Mississippi after sailing ships phased out
evidence.quote: After wooden sailing ships were phased out this land was transferred to the State of Mississippi a 100 years ago as an endowment for the University of Mississippi.

evidence.supports: managed as University Forest Lands until 2000 Congress purchase; tower came with tract
evidence.quote: It was managed as University Forest Lands until 2000 when Congress purchased the tract for addition to the DeSoto National Forest. With this tract came the University Fire Tower

evidence.supports: no longer in service; Forest Service maintains it for emergencies
evidence.quote: It is no longer in service but is maintained by the U.S. Forest Service for emergencies.

evidence.supports: nominated by a district ranger, De Soto Ranger District
location: De Soto National Forest, Stone County, Mississippi
De Soto Ranger District listed as cooperator

sources.title: University Lookout Tower
sources.publisher: National Historic Lookout Register (American Resources, Inc. and Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Single source: the NHLR register entry, which gives the design, the 2000 Congress purchase of the tract for the De Soto National Forest, the no-longer-in-service status and the Forest Service's emergency maintenance, but no build year. No staffing, fire or repair history was found. The register gives no public access information; the story asks visitors not to climb and to ask the De Soto Ranger District, which the register lists as a cooperator. The 2000 purchase is taken from the register only; a Forest Service or Federal Register source would confirm it. Two WebSearch queries and two register reads were used. Record design is null and can take the design fact.
